html:
Converts to Christianity killed on the orders of Mwanga II, the Kabaka (king) of Buganda, between 1885 and 1887.

Anglican and Catholic missionaries had reached Buganda in the late 1870s, and Islam had come earlier. Many converts were young pages at the royal court. Mwanga feared that the new faiths and their foreign backers were undermining his power, and he saw the pages' refusals to obey him as defiance. In 1885 he had the Anglican bishop James Hannington killed. In 1886 he ordered a wave of killings; the largest group was burned alive at Namugongo on 3 June.

The Catholic martyrs, led by Charles Lwanga, were made saints by Pope Paul VI in 1964, among the first saints from sub-Saharan Africa. The Anglican martyrs are honoured too. Every 3 June huge crowds of pilgrims walk to Namugongo from across East Africa.
sum: Converts to Christianity killed on the orders of Mwanga II, the Kabaka (king) of Buganda, between 1885 and 1887.
